heading: Top two. One more round.
text: On August 18, District 1 voters put Linda Cothiere Aristide in the top two out of seven candidates. Thank you to every voter, every volunteer, and every neighbor who knocked a door, made a call, or planted a sign to get us here. The race now goes to the general election on Tuesday, November 3 — and every registered voter in District 1 gets a say.

heading: Raised in Carol City. Rooted in District 1.
text: Linda Cothiere Aristide was born in Cap-Haïtien, Haiti, and came to Miami as a child. Like so many District 1 families, she started out in a public school before she had the language — and came up through it anyway: she grew up in Carol City and graduated from Miami Carol City Senior High. A proud product of Miami-Dade public schools, she earned her associate degree at Miami Dade College and her bachelor's in education at St. Thomas University, then gave her career back to the community that raised her — building adult-education programs that move our neighbors into real careers.

heading: Raised in Carol City. Rooted in District 1.
text: She is a certified mediator. She is a Deaconess at Good News Church of North Miami — school-supply drives, food distributions, Thanksgiving turkeys, holiday toys. And for the past five years she has talked with South Florida every week, co-hosting The Reyni Talk Show on 1360 AM.

heading: Raised in Carol City. Rooted in District 1.
text: At home, education is the family business: her husband, Wallace Aristide, served Miami-Dade schools for more than 30 years — over a decade of them as principal of Miami Northwestern Senior High.

heading: Raised in Carol City. Rooted in District 1.

heading: Empower teachers in the classroom
text: Cut the bureaucratic overload and give educators the tools, autonomy, and professional trust they have earned — so their time goes to students, not paperwork.

heading: Safe & modern campuses
text: "You can't learn where you don't feel safe."

heading: Safe & modern campuses
text: Security infrastructure, modernized facilities, and updated classroom technology — every campus in District 1 safe, cool, and 21st-century ready.

heading: Parents as partners
text: Parents are a child's first educators — informed, included, and at the table before decisions are made, with real access in every family's language.

heading: Pay & keep great teachers
text: Florida ranks last in the nation for teacher pay, and we lose ours to the next county. Direct local dollars to competitive pay and real retention — the smartest investment we can make.

heading: What that looks like on the board
text: A School Board member sets policy, adopts a $7.4 billion budget, hires and holds the Superintendent accountable, approves contracts, sets the salary schedule, draws attendance boundaries, and decides when schools open or close. Here is how Linda will use that authority — and where she will fight in Tallahassee for what the state controls.

heading: 1 · Empower teachers
text: Audit district-mandated paperwork and cut duplicative reporting so teachers teach, not document.

heading: 1 · Empower teachers
text: Protect classroom autonomy and professional judgment within state standards.

heading: 1 · Empower teachers
text: Seat working District 1 teachers on the advisory committees that shape curriculum and scheduling.

heading: 2 · Safe & modern campuses
text: Verify every District 1 school meets Florida's Marjory Stoneman Douglas safety law — a safe-school officer, single point of entry, and an Alyssa's Law panic alarm in every building.

heading: 2 · Safe & modern campuses
text: Demand a District 1 accounting of the 2012 $1.2 billion school bond — continuing the audit the seat's own former member called for — so we know our buildings, A/C, and technology got their fair share.

heading: 2 · Safe & modern campuses
text: Prioritize cooling, repairs, and updated classroom technology in the capital plan.

heading: 3 · Parents as partners
text: Require genuine parent notice and input before any District 1 school is closed, consolidated, or rezoned — not after the vote.

heading: 3 · Parents as partners
text: Strengthen communication in every family's language — English, Kreyòl, and Español — through the Parent Portal and Parent Academy.

heading: 3 · Parents as partners

heading: 4 · Pay & keep great teachers
text: Protect and prioritize the voter-approved teacher-salary referendum — up for renewal on this term — toward competitive pay and retention.

heading: 4 · Pay & keep great teachers
text: Close the pay and working-condition gap with neighboring counties so we stop losing great teachers.

heading: 4 · Pay & keep great teachers
text: Fight in Tallahassee for a real state investment in teacher salaries — Florida currently ranks 50th in the nation.

heading: Nine schools closed. One vote. No debate.
text: Two of them are District 1 schools. Fly the real map: watch the children cross it, see exactly what the vote did, and meet the neighbor running to answer it.

heading: One seat. Four communities.
text: District 1 stretches across Miami Gardens, Opa-locka, North Miami and North Miami Beach. One board seat speaks for all of them — and every family in them deserves a champion who shows up. Together, these neighborhoods are part of Miami-Dade County Public Schools — one of the nation's largest, A-rated districts.

heading: The election, plainly answered.
text: In the first round on August 18, 2026, no candidate won a majority, and Linda Cothiere Aristide finished in the top two . The race now goes to the general election on Tuesday, November 3, 2026 . School board races are nonpartisan, so every registered voter in District 1 votes in November.

heading: The election, plainly answered.
text: Linda Cothiere Aristide is a classroom teacher with more than a decade in Miami-Dade public school classrooms and a lifetime in District 1. She grew up in Carol City, graduated from Miami Carol City Senior High, and earned her degrees at Miami Dade College and St. Thomas University. She is not a stranger to these schools — she is a product of them.

heading: The election, plainly answered.
text: District 1 covers Miami Gardens, Opa-locka, North Miami and North Miami Beach — 33 public schools within Miami-Dade County Public Schools, one of the largest school districts in the nation.

heading: The election, plainly answered.
text: Request a vote-by-mail ballot from the Miami-Dade Supervisor of Elections at votemiamidade.gov or by calling 305-499-8683. Requests must be renewed each election cycle — even if you voted by mail in August, confirm your request is active for November 3, 2026.

heading: How to vote in the November 3 runoff
text: Linda Cothiere Aristide faces Katrina Wilson in the runoff. Here's how to register, vote by mail, or vote on Election Day.

heading: How to vote in the November 3 runoff
text: #92 Punch On your ballot, Linda Cothiere Aristide is #92 . Find the School Board District 1 race and mark #92 .

heading: Sites and dates are coming in late October
text: Miami-Dade County has not yet published the early-voting schedule for the November 3, 2026 general election. The county typically releases early-voting sites and hours about two to three weeks before Election Day. Check back here, or go straight to the county's page.

heading: Sites and dates are coming in late October
text: Once early voting opens, a Secure Ballot Intake Station is staffed at every early-voting site during voting hours, so you can drop off a vote-by-mail ballot in person instead of mailing it.
